transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Rossi (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Head of ML, Elk Ignite), Sam Ortiz (Platform Eng), Lena Kowalski (Security), Tomás Ribeiro (Data Eng), Ava Miller (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen):
- Pilot agreed: chat embeddings + re-ranking for internal search.
- Private/VPC deployment preferred, fallback to dedicated hosted if network constraints.
- Data residency: EU for training logs, US for telemetry; KMS integration required.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Okay, hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll call — we'll do a short intro then jump into scope. {laughter} Um, if you could do a one-line on your role that helps.
[00:18] Priya Nair (Elk Ignite): Hi, Priya here — Head of ML, I'll own success criteria and evaluation for the pilot. We're trying to move from our prototype to something production-grade.
[00:28] Sam Ortiz (Elk Ignite): Sam — platform eng, I'll own networking and staging. Couple firewall quirks on our side.
[00:34] Lena Kowalski (Elk Ignite): Lena, security — I'll be the main reviewer for KMS and audit logs.
[00:40] Jordan Lee: Great. Diego, quick intro?
[00:45] Diego Chen (Redwood): Hey all, Diego here — SE, focus on inference performance and deployment patterns. We'll want to baseline latency and throughput, and run a small benchmark.
[00:52] [00:52] Tomás Ribeiro (Elk Ignite): Tomás — data eng, I'll handle ingestion pipelines and sample data.
[00:58] Ava Miller (Elk Ignite): Ava product — aligning pilot goals to product KPIs.

[01:10] Jordan Lee: Cool. Agenda — confirm pilot scope, exchange network/security constraints, agree SLOs and timeline. Priya, can you outline the success criteria?
[01:22] Priya Nair: Sure — primary is 95th pct latency under 400ms for chat flows at our expected QPS, embedding generation under 200ms, and a cost target that's below our current managed vendor by 30%. Also quality gating — we have a small labeled eval set we want to pass.
[01:45] Diego Chen: Quick clarifier — is that 95th pct token-latency or response-latency? Sometimes those differ a bit depending on batching.
[01:52] Priya Nair: Response latency is what matters.

[02:10] Jordan Lee: Okay — that's helpful. On deployment model, you mentioned preferring private. Sam, can you walk us through constraints?
[02:20] Sam Ortiz: Yes. We run in a VPC inside AWS in eu-west-1. We're open to peering or transit gateway. Firewall rules are pretty strict — only outbound to a handful of IPs. Also our infra team prefers not to open wide egress to public endpoints.
[02:40] Diego Chen: Understood. Redwood has both Dedicated and Private options — Private means a customer-managed VPC connector and our control plane access constrained by SSO. Dedicated is hosted in our tenant but with reserved capacity. Both can hit your SLOs but Private reduces data egress concerns.
[02:58] Priya Nair: If the Private option requires on-prem hardware or non-standard installs that's a blocker — we need to avoid long procurement.
[03:08] Jordan Lee: Right, most customers do Private via VPC peering and shared control plane; on-prem package exists but only for highly regulated. We should confirm the exact network routes.

[03:30] [03:30] Lena Kowalski: For security — KMS integration is mandatory. We use AWS KMS CMKs with key policies restricted to our security team. Also we need audit logs for every inference request for the pilot. Any way Redwood can surface request-level logs without token content leakage?
[03:52] Diego Chen: Yes — we support envelope encryption and can redact payloads in logs. For request-level tracing we can provide metadata (request id, model, latencies) while redacting user content. We'll send the security pack that explains that.
[04:12] Jordan Lee: We'll add a section in the SOW for KMS and audit-log handling.

[04:30] Priya Nair: About model choice — we're using a trimmed 7B for now; we want to evaluate quantization to S4/INT8 to meet latency. Is that in-scope?
[04:42] Diego Chen: Absolutely. We can provision a quantized variant for the pilot. Quick note: quantization may change output tokenization slightly, so we'll pair it with your eval set to ensure quality.
[04:57] Priya Nair: Good — we can't afford quality regressions.

[05:10] Jordan Lee: Timeline proposal: Week 0 (this week) — SOW + staging tenant access; Week 1 — provisioning + baseline benchmarks; Week 2 — tuning (quantization, batching); Week 3 — pilot evaluation and handoff. Does that track?
[05:25] Ava Miller: Sounds tight but doable. We might need more runway on our infra side for networking approvals.
[05:31] Sam Ortiz: Agree — I can start the peering request today but approvals usually take 5 business days.

[06:00] Diego Chen: For the baseline benchmarks we need: sample QPS, avg/peak concurrent sessions, typical sequence lengths (prompt + response tokens), and a small labeled eval. If you can drop that in the shared spreadsheet we'll kick off the harness.
[06:20] Tomás Ribeiro: I'll populate that by EOD tomorrow.

[06:40] Jordan Lee: Great. Any procurement/legal items we should be aware of?
[06:45] Lena Kowalski: NDA is already in place. Our procurement expects a standard MSA for Dedicated, but for Private deployment there may be additional network addendums. Also we require SOC2 Type 2 and ISO mentions in the vendor pack.
[07:02] Jordan Lee: We include SOC2 attestation in our security docs; I'll attach the certs and the compliance matrix.

[07:30] [07:30] Priya Nair: Quick note on observability — we need token-level cost breakdowns per request and per-route latency histograms. Is that available in the Console?
[07:42] Maya Rossi (Redwood): Yes — Redwood Console exposes per-route and per-model dashboards, token breakdowns, and traces. For pilots we can give 90-day retention on telemetry.
[07:55] Priya Nair: Ok, good.

[08:10] Jordan Lee: Let's talk about success metrics again — QA gating with your labeled set; can you share the pass/fail thresholds?
[08:20] Priya Nair: We'll aim for F1 over 0.82 on the retrieval+rerank eval; for chat we'll do a human A/B on a 100-example set with a net preference >55% for Redwood outputs vs baseline.
[08:35] Diego Chen: We'll instrument the eval harness to run these comparisons and produce a simple report.

[09:00] Sam Ortiz: Network practicals — what IP ranges do we need to allow for peering?
[09:07] Jordan Lee: I'll share a minimal list — Redwood control plane and dedicated egress ranges; for Private peering, traffic stays in your VPC and our worker subnets are in a customer-managed subnet. We'll provide a diagram.

[09:30] [09:30] Lena Kowalski: One more — retention: how long do logs with metadata live in the Redwood tenant by default and can we shorten it?
[09:38] Maya Rossi: Default is 90 days for telemetry, but for pilot customers we can configure retention to 30 days. We'll note that in the SOW.

[10:00] Jordan Lee: Any blockers on the data classification front? Priya?
[10:05] Priya Nair: A few prompts contain minimal PII; we'll flag those and provide a scrubbed dataset. That's fine for pilot.

[10:20] Diego Chen: Ok, moving to benchmarks — sample harness will test: cold start latency, steady-state throughput with batching, and a KV cache prefix test for chat continuity. Expect initial numbers but will refine after tuning.

[11:00] Priya Nair: Will you support model pinning across rollout so we can rollback to a non-quantized variant if needed?
[11:08] Diego Chen: Yes — Redwood supports model pinning and rollout policies, can do canary with traffic split and automatic fallback.

[11:30] Jordan Lee: Good. Questions from customer?
[11:35] Ava Miller: Who is the day-to-day contact at Redwood for incident escalation?
[11:40] Maya Rossi: That'll be me; I'll be the CSM and primary contact for the pilot. Diego will be the SE contact for technical escalations. Jordan covers commercial.

[12:00] [12:00] Tomás Ribeiro: Small question on cost accounting — do you provide per-request tokenized cost numbers or an aggregated bucket?
[12:08] Diego Chen: We provide per-request token breakdowns and cost allocation tags. You can tag by route or team.

[12:30] Jordan Lee: Alright let's do a quick recap and agreed next steps.
[12:35] Jordan Lee: Action items — I'll send the SOW and security pack; Diego will send benchmark harness; Tomás will provide traffic profiles; Sam will start peering request; Lena will confirm KMS vendor. We'll aim to have staging access by end of Week 1.

[12:58] Priya Nair: Thanks everyone — excited to move forward.
[13:05] Jordan Lee: Same — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the Week 2 deep-dive.

[47:20] [wrap-up] Maya Rossi: I'll create a shared folder with all artifacts: SOW draft, security pack, benchmark spreadsheet and invite the team. Expect that in the next 24 hours.
[47:34] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Thanks all — meeting adjourned.
